findings.element: .b-step buttons and the .b-item they edit (render-b.js, states["owner-editing"].move)
findings.problem: The gesture this whole direction exists for tells the truth in one place out of four. Driven at 1440: before the press the row reads count 23, date SAT 8 AUG, accessible name "Send the invitations, Saturday 8 August, in 23 days", readout "Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days". After a single press of "Move a week earlier" the count reads 16 and the item slides up the measure, but .b-date still reads SAT 8 AUG, the .b-grab accessible name still says "Saturday 8 August, in 23 days", and the .b-stepRead readout drops the date entirely to "in 16 days" — so the one field naming the date being changed stops naming a date the instant you change it. A keyboard or screen-reader user hears the old date read back after every move. move() writes a bare day-offset instead of a new date, so nothing derived from the date can follow it. The gate passes this because it only asserts readout.includes(String(away)).
findings.fix: In move(), stop carrying an offset and compute a real date: var iso = new Date(Date.UTC(2026,6,16) + current*86400000).toISOString().slice(0,10). Then rewrite every fact about the item from that one value in the same frame — item.querySelector('.b-away').textContent = String(current); item.querySelector('.b-date').textContent = F.fmt.weekdayShort(iso)+' '+F.fmt.short(iso); item.querySelector('.b-grab').setAttribute('aria-label', title+', '+F.fmt.long(iso)+', in '+current+' days. '+visibility+'. Open to change it.'); read.textContent = F.fmt.longYear(iso)+' · in '+current+' days' — keeping the date in the readout at every value, not only the first. Add an assertion to interaction-check.mjs that after one −7 and after one +1 the count, the .b-date line, the .b-grab accessible name and the .b-stepRead all name the same single date.

findings.problem: The measure's stated law — strictly proportional, no two items ever touching — survives exactly one press. Clicking "Move a week earlier" once puts the invitations at 16 days, the same day as the menu tasting, and the two rows render at identical tops (both offsetTop 224, both rects t=467): "Menu tasting at The Orchard" and "Send the invitations" print as one unreadable smear of overlapping glyphs, SAT 8 AUG over SAT 1 AUG, two SHOWN chips stacked. The other direction has no ceiling at all: twelve presses of +7 put the item 107 days out — past the wedding day at 79, and 300px below the bottom of a .b-measure whose height is fixed at the horizon (top 1498 against a height of 1198) — while the horizon still reads 79. The surface will let an owner place something after the day the whole page is measured to, and says nothing. The gate's collision and proportion assertions run only at first paint, never after the gesture.
findings.fix: Clamp move() to 1…F.toDay(), and set aria-disabled="true" plus a one-line note "The day itself is 79 days away" on the + buttons at the ceiling rather than silently absorbing the press. Then run a collision pass after every move: measure each .b-item rect, and where the moved item lands within 8px of a neighbour, merge the pair into one same-day row — a single count, a single tick, both titles stacked inside that row — instead of two absolutely-positioned boxes at the same top. Add assertions to interaction-check.mjs that after any sequence of stepper presses no two .b-item rects overlap, no item's offsetTop exceeds the measure's height, and no item's count exceeds the horizon count.

findings.element: .b-edit (b.css) and its host .b-item on the measure
findings.problem: The rule above .b-edit says "It gets an opaque ground so nothing reads through." It does not. background: var(--back) is declared and then re-declared as background: var(--fore-06) seven lines later at the same specificity, so the panel paints rgba(255,255,255,0.06) and three rows of the plan — fitting, music, guests — read straight through it at full brightness while the panel's own labels sit behind them. It is visible in the shipped owner-editing frame at 1440, where "Final dress fitting" prints across "What guests see". Because the editor floats out of an absolutely-positioned item, no band is reserved for it at any width. At 390 — the device the flagship owner is actually holding — the panel is 154px wide and 537px tall, the title input clips to "Send the inv", the four steppers wrap into two rows around the readout, "Take it off the plan" wraps to three lines, and four rows of the plan read through the whole thing. The gate opens owner-editing only at 1440.
findings.fix: Delete the second background declaration on .b-edit so the declared opaque var(--back) stands, and add box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--fore-16) so it separates from the rail. Then give it real layout instead of floating it: at [data-medium="full"] and [data-medium="sheet"], reserve a 360px right gutter on .b-measure (padding-right:360px) and position .b-edit inside that gutter at the edited item's own top, so the panel occupies reserved space and can never stand over a row while still sitting level with the item it edits. Below 560px there is no gutter, so render .b-edit as position:fixed;inset:auto 0 0 0 — a full-width sheet on the bottom of the viewport with the input, stepper and actions each on their own row — and scroll the edited item to sit above it. Add assertions that .b-edit's computed background alpha is 1 and that its rect intersects no other .b-item rect, at 390, 768 and 1440.

findings.problem: The reversibility surface is a still life. On load, before anything has been touched, the live region already announces "Last change: the invitations moved seven days closer." — a change that has not happened, read out to a screen-reader user the moment the page arrives. Clicking its Undo button changes nothing (the count stays 23). The Ctrl Z printed in its own kbd element is not bound: pressing it changes nothing. And after a real move the region does not update at all — it still reads "moved seven days closer" after a +7. So the one surface promising a way back neither records what happened nor offers one, and it is printed on screen advertising a keystroke that does not exist. The gate asserts the region exists, is role=status, holds a button and names a key; every one of those is true and none of it works.
findings.fix: Keep a history array in states["owner-editing"]; have move() push {id, fromIso, toIso} and re-render .b-undo from the last entry, naming the real change ("Send the invitations moved from Saturday 8 August to Saturday 1 August"). Render nothing in the region until history is non-empty rather than pre-loading a fiction. Wire the Undo button and a document keydown listener for (e.ctrlKey||e.metaKey) && e.key === 'z' to pop the last entry, re-apply it through the same move() path, and return focus to the .b-step that made the change. Add assertions that .b-undo is empty at rest, names the real change after one move, and that Ctrl+Z restores the item's exact top, count, .b-date and accessible name.

findings.element: .b-item rows, the .b-grab chip and the .b-seg visibility control
findings.problem: Nothing on the measure looks touchable, and the two things that are do nothing. The row has no hover, no focus-within, no cursor change and no background at rest (computed background rgba(0,0,0,0), cursor auto); the only way into editing is a 54x28 mono chip set in 11px uppercase at 62% ink reading SHOWN, which at rest reads as a status badge rather than a door — and clicking it does nothing at all, the DOM is byte-identical after the click. Meanwhile the highest-stakes control an owner ever touches, the "On the plan / Kept private" segmented group, does not press: after clicking "Kept private", aria-pressed is still true on "On the plan" and false on "Kept private", and the row's chip still reads SHOWN. A person deciding whether their guests can see something gets no evidence they decided anything. Separately the rows are announced into nothing: .b-measure carries role="list" and contains zero role="listitem" children, so a screen reader reports a list with no items and all seven rows fall outside it.
findings.fix: Make the row the control: replace .b-grab with a full-row button.b-open carrying the existing accessible name, with the SHOWN/PRIVATE chip as its right-aligned content, and give .b-item a treatment at rest-to-hover — .b-item:hover, .b-item:focus-within { background: var(--fore-04) } bled 12px each side with negative margin plus matching padding, transitioned at var(--t-fast) var(--ease) so nothing reflows. Wire the .b-seg buttons to swap aria-pressed on click and to rewrite both the chip text and the row's accessible name from the same accessor, so the visibility fact exists in words wherever it exists in ink. Add role="listitem" to each .b-item so the seven rows sit inside the list they are announced as, and assert in interaction-check.mjs that the listitem count equals the ahead() count and that clicking "Kept private" flips aria-pressed on both buttons and changes the row's chip and accessible name.

biggestWin: 6.3. What earned it: at rest this is genuinely studio-grade, and the states nobody screenshots are the best ones. The loading frame refuses to draw a measure whose tick positions are among the things still loading and says so in words, with no shimmer and no invented sections — the single strongest thing here, and most products get it wrong. Focus hygiene is real: eleven named stops on the owner surface, nothing invisible focusable, focus stays scrolled into view through every move, one outline-only focus rule, and reduced motion removes every transition rather than most of them. Ended, day, print and publish are finished. What stands between it and 9.5 is not polish, it is a build, and it is one object: the editor. Every finding above lives in the fifteen seconds an owner spends changing a date. The thesis is that a pixel is a real unit of time and that moving a date is pulling something nearer — and the moment you pull, two rows land on top of each other in an unreadable smear, the row keeps reading out its old date, the readout stops naming any date, the panel paints six-percent white so the plan reads through it, undo announces a change that never happened, and on a 390px phone the whole editor is 154px wide with four rows of the plan showing through it. At rest this is a 9; under the hand it is a 5, and my seat grades it under the hand. The build is roughly two days: make move() write a date instead of an offset and re-derive every fact from it, clamp and de-collide the measure, give the editor a reserved gutter at desk width and a bottom sheet on a phone, and make undo real. None of it was caught because the gate opens the editor at one width and presses the stepper once; grow those assertions in the same pass or round two will rediscover this list.
